tossups.text: this structure is essential for brainstem structures. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cerebrum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cerebrum is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in brainstem structures.

tossups.text: This novel alludes to Billy Budd when the protagonist experiences the "orgasm of the hanged man" in a police station. It was originally printed together with a Maurice Helbrant novel, and its cover illustration depicted a man struggling with a screaming blonde woman for a packet in her hand in front of a table with a stove on it. This novel portrays Herbert Huncke in the character of Herman, and its loose sequel, which also deals with the search for yagé with which this novel concludes, is entitled Queer. This novel is presented as the memoir of its pseudonymous author, William Lee. For 10 points, name these "Confessions of an Unredeemed Drug Addict," the first novel by William S. Burroughs.

This poet wrote, "You may mock the hapless plight / or the creatures of your use" in a poem that describes figures "perverse, schooled to condemn... by witless laws." The line "'Tis dead, 'tis dust, 'tis shadow, yea, 'tis nought" concludes this poet's "To Her Portrait." In one poem, this poet discussed a figure "roused by her own precipitous fall" who "crowns herself with the globe's abandoned half" before noting, "the world illuminated, / and I awake." This poet of "Arraignment of the Men" discussed the "pyramidal death-born shadow of earth" in a silva analyzed in Octavio Paz's The Traps of Faith. This poet condemned the Church for keeping women uneducated following criticism from the Bishop of Puebla in her "Reply to Sister Philotea." For 10 points, name this author of First Dream, a 17th-century Mexican nun.
acceptableAnswers: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
Juana Inés de Asbaje y Ramírez de Santillana

tossups.text: After being left by these people in Colchester, the title character of a Defoe story is raised by a "very house" woman. Along with Primitivo, another of these people is the only member of Pablo's gang who goes with Robert to survive the final attack in For Whom the Bell Tolls. This type of person is told "Go, for they call you, Shepherd, from the hill" in a companion poem to "Thyrsis," written by Matthew Arnold. After pushing Frollo to his death, a son of these people lies down next to his love, who was adopted by them. For 10 points, name this nomadic ethnic group exemplified by Esméralda in The Hunchback of Notre Dame, who are sometimes called Roma.

this structure is essential for hypothalamic hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in hypothalamic hormones.

tossups.text: At the start of this event, one figure threw his shield down so that he would not be the first person to land on enemy soil. That man attempted to avoid this event by sowing his fields with salt in order to feign madness. The horses of Rhesus were killed by Diomedes in this event before they could drink from the Xanthus river. That action, along with the death of Troilus, were part of a prophecy fating a city to fall in this event. The prophet Laocoon was killed in this conflict. Sparked by the Judgement of Paris, For 10 points, name this mythological conflict in which Greeks used a wooden horse to take over a certain city.

When the Froude number is supercritical, cross laminations in this material will form "anti" structures which drift forward. Deflation causes this substance to "skip" along the surface in the process of saltation. This substance can form "transverse," "star," or crescent-shaped "barchan" structures. The slip faces of those structures made of this material have an angle of repose of 34 degrees. It's not soil, but an equal proportion of silt, clay, and this material forms loam. High levels of basalt can result in a black example of this substance that is common in Hawai'i. For 10 points, name this granular substance that forms characteristic "dunes" in deserts.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on soil before “soil” is read

tossups.text: These functions can be rescaled using Schmidt semi-normalization. The standard proof of Unsöld's theorem relies on these functions' namesake addition theorem. Applying the spin raising and lowering operators to these functions gives their "spin-weighted" variety, which can be used to find multipole solutions of Maxwell's equations in a source-free region. The Slater integral of the product of three of these functions is proportional to the product of two Wigner three-j symbols. The simplest of these functions equals the square root of one over four pi. They are the eigenfunctions of the L-squared and L-sub-z operators. To within a normalization factor, the product of one of these functions and an associated Laguerre polynomial gives the wavefunction of the hydrogen atom. For 10 points, identify these functions denoted Y-sub-l-super-m that solve the angular part of Laplace's equation in their namesake coordinate system.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on any of those answers thereafter

tossups.text: Carl Nielsen's third work of this type is named Espansiva. Camille Saint-Saens wrote three of these works, including one named for the organ. Many Classical period examples of these had their fast first movements written in sonata form. Mozart's last one of these works is his No. 41, and was known as the Jupiter. Mahler wrote one of these works that required so many performers that it was often called one of these works of A Thousand. For 10 points, name these large-scale works for orchestra that included Berlioz' Fantastique and Dvorak's From The New World.

Regarding this structure, the architect Louis Kahn once remarked, "The sun did not know how beautiful its light was until it was reflected off this building." Inspired by the subtle grain of Japanese ceramics, the designer of this building hired Höganäs to create similar clay tiles to match both his vision and his "Spherical Solution" for the roof of this building. The architect Peter Hall made changes to the interior design of the auditorium seating in this building, to fit legal requirements. Jørn Utzon designed, for 10 points, what building with white, sail-like, interlocking arches, located in Australia?

Construction began in 312 BC, when the Roman army was being soundly defeated by the Samnites during the Second Samnite War. Named after a Roman censor who was noted for his public works projects, it was built with a swell in the middle to allow water to run off the sides, and it had ditches on both sides to collect the water. The emperor Trajan would later build the Via Traiana in order to reach by a shorter route. For 10 points, identify this "queen of the long roads" leading to from the Roman coliseum.

Anderson and Goulden developed a truck-based platform to measure this phenomenon regionally, whereas Richard Allen and Wim Bastiaanssen developed the METRIC and SEBAL models to estimate it using satellite and ground data. The Hargreaves and Blaney-Criddle equations are older empirical methods to estimate it, while the GRACE satellite can calculate it as a residual if other processes in the cycle involving it are known. C.W. Thornthwaite mapped the global potential of it, while the FAO recommends using an equation named after Penman and Montieth to estimate the reference variety of it. Most accurately measured using a lysimeter, it can be calculated by dividing latent energy by the heat of vaporization. For 10 points, name this phenomenon which estimates water removed from both bare surface and plants by vaporization.

This battle began after one side refused to allow the opposing commander to make a sacrifice at the temple of Melkart. The tactics used in this battle were used in the same year against Batis at the Battle of Gaza. 2000 members of the defeated army were nailed to crosses on the beach at the end of this battle, though King Azemilcus was spared. During this battle a ship full of combustible materials were launched against two gigantic towers with catapults on top and ballistas on the bottom. The victorious side in this battle created a one-kilometer long causeway upon which gigantic siege engines bombarded the target city. For 10 points, name this 6-month battle in 332 BCE in which Alexander the Great besieged and captured a Phonecian city.

A three-membered ring containing a cation of this element is nucleophilically attacked by acetate to form a vicinal diol in the Woodward cis-hydroxylation. An acid of this element and oxygen is used to cleave vicinal diols into carbonyls. This element binds to 7 fluorine atoms in a classical example of a pentagonal bipyramidal compound. This is the largest element that can bind to silver in a chemical used in photographic film. Deficiency of this element in the human body leads to an enlarged thyroid, a condition known as goiter. This element is used to test for starch by staining it a blue-black color. The only diatomic element to be solid at room temperature, for 10 points, name this second-heaviest halogen, whose chemical symbol is I.

The similarity between two of these objects can be given by the Levenstein distance. The set of all of these over a given set V is given by the Kleene Star of V, and The Boyer-Moore and Rabin-Karp algorithms can be used to search them. The Lempel-Ziv-Welch compression algorithm creates a translation table of these objects upon initialization, and fixed-length ones can be plotted as nodes on a hypercube. The trim function removes trailing whitespace from these variables, and analyzing them with respect to a given formal grammar is known as parsing. Also the subject of regular expressions, concatenation is the combining of, For 10 points, what type of variable which stores an ordered sequence of symbols, most commonly used to store text?

This religion believes that one may "overstand" something while not understanding it. Its eating practices are heavily based on Revelation 22:2, which speaks of the "leaves of the tree" and the "healing of the nation." It is based on the teachings of Howell and meets for Groundings where reasonings occur. Its adherents celebrate the holiday of Nyabingi and follow a strict dietary code known as Ital. The Lion of Judah is sacred to this religion along with texts like The Promise Key and The Holy Piby. Babylon is an oppressive force that is contrasted with Zion in this religion that reveres Hailie Selassie. For 10 points, name this Jah-worshipping religion that ritually smokes ganja.

One type of this process occurs after an object gains enough layers of differing transparency through random motion that it cannot be supported. Rising thermals can drive adiabatic cooling that causes this process, as can orographic lift, the latter of which can result in a "shadow" on the far side of mountains. Objects that are either large and anvil-shaped or dark sheets are called "nimbus" for supporting this process. For 10 points, nimbostratus and cumulonimbus clouds cause what process in which water falls from the sky?

The protagonist of this film declares, "I can be smart when it's important" and is attracted to Piggy Beekman, who is in the mining business. In its best known number, men dance with women wearing pink dresses as the singer declares, "a kiss on the hand may be grand, but it won't pay the rental on your humble flat". A "little girl from Little Rock" named Dorothy Shaw was played by Jane Russell in this film. Based on a novel by Anita Loos, it features the song, "Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend". For 10 points, name this 1953 musical starring Marilyn Monroe, based on a novel whose sequel noted that the title people "Marry Brunettes".

The construction of this entity was first proposed by Asa Whitney and Theodore Judah. The Big Four, including Leland Stanford, helped finance it. It was revealed that its construction costs were too high in the Crédit Mobilier scandal. Its construction was aided by many Chinese immigrants with dynamite and came to end at Promontory Point, Utah with the driving of the Golden Spike. Name this railroad constructed by Central Pacific and Union Pacific that linked the coasts of America.

This ruler intentionally aggravated Bishop Sotern by sending an army to destroy the Udenheim fortress built near his borders. The fanatic "mad halberstadter" Christian the Younger raised an army for this ruler, who lost his allies' support in the Treaty of Ulm. This ruler commissioned Salomon de Caus and Inigo Jones to build him a garden called the "eighth wonder of the world." James I of England formed an ill-considered alliance with this man by allowing him to marry his daughter, Elizabeth Stuart. This father of Prince Rupert of the Rhine was crowned in Prague in 1619 and subsequently attacked by the forces of the Catholic League under Count von Tilly. For 10 points, name this Protestant king from the Thirty Years' War whose defeat at the Battle of White Mountain ended his brief rule over Bohemia.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with spleen functions.
What is the main function of the lymph in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to spleen functions.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Give this two-word superlative, which appears in the first sentence of a novel subtitled "A Tale of Passion" before a description of a stay in Nauheim, where the narrator's wife feigns heart disease to conceal her affair.
acceptableAnswers: “This is the saddest story I have ever heard”

parts.text: The line "this is the saddest story I have ever heard" opens this author's 1915 novel about the Dowells and the Ashburnhams. This author also wrote the Parade's End tetralogy.

Arthur Mizener's biography The Saddest Story reads the character Florence Dowell as inspired by Ford's affair with Violet Hunt, who also inspired the adulterer Norah Nesbit in this author's novel Of Human Bondage.

bonuses.leadin: In a dedication to his wife Stella Bowen, an author described how he had intended this phrase to title his "best book" but was urged otherwise by his publisher due to its association with "the darkest days of war." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author, whom Bill Buford identified as the "godfather" of "dirty realism." The alter ego Henry Chinaski was introduced in this author's novel Post Office.
Bukowski set much of his misanthropic fiction in this city, his longtime home. John Fante's Ask the Dust is set in this city, as is F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Last Tycoon.

Detective Nicky Belane tries to find author Louis-Ferdinand Céline in a Bukowski novel titled for this adjective, which describes cheap magazines of lowbrow stories. "The Gold Watch" is part of Roger Avary's screenplay for a Quentin Tarantino film titled for this kind of Fiction.

bonuses.leadin: Anecdotally, this author went around yelling "I am Arturo Bandini!" in reference to John Fante's literary alter ego. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Spanish author of romances like Persiles and Sigismunda.
Cervantes' most famous work is probably this novel about a windmill-battling man who journeys with Sancho Panza as a knight-errant in search of adventure.
This book, Cervantes' first, tells the story of Elico and Eriso's love for the title character. The opening scene of the novel shows her and Florisa bathing.

bonuses.leadin: His Journey To Parnassus pokes fun at his contemporaries, and he published a series of Exemplary Novels alongside his more famous works. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with lung volumes and capacities.
What is the main function of the diaphragm in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to lung volumes and capacities.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name these things, one of which was destroyed by Saint Boniface (BAH-nif-us). Ratatoskr (RAT-uh-tosk-ur) carried messages on a mythical one of these objects.
This chief god of the Norse pantheon hanged himself on the world tree Yggdrasil (IG-drus-il) for nine days in order to understand the runes.
Yggdrasil is attested in the Völuspá (VOO-loosh-poh) section of this Old Norse literary work. Much of this originally untitled work was preserved in the Codex Regius.

bonuses.leadin: In western Norway, ale was poured over the Warden example of these things as part of a yearly festival. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this collection of three laws of motion, the second of which states that force equals mass times acceleration. They were formulated by a man who discovered a law of universal gravitation after an apple hit him.
Another formulation of Newton's Second Law states that force is the derivative with respect to time of this quantity, equal to mass times velocity.

Newton's third law follows from Noether's Theorem, which roughly states that there is a law of this type for most physical processes. One of these laws for kinetic energy only applies in the case of elastic collisions.

bonuses.leadin: One of these states that every action causes an equal and opposite reaction. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these bacteria that rely on oxygen provided by leg·hemoglobin in root nodules. These nitrogen-fixing bacteria live in symbiotic relationships with legumes.
Nitrogenases in rhizobia fix atmospheric nitrogen into this compound and a similar ion with an additional proton.

Lectins and these compounds in root exudates help establish rhizobia-legume symbiosis. Phenyl·alanine is a precursor to these polyphenolic compounds, whose subgroups include chalcones, anthocyanins, and condensed tannins.

bonuses.leadin: These soil bacteria secrete Nod factors, which induce root hair elongation and the formation of an infection thread. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this country, led by the Pope of the Catholic Church.
This church in the Vatican had its ceiling painted by Michelangelo.
The entire country of Vatican City is located completely within this other city.

bonuses.leadin: This country was formed by the 1929 Lateran Treaty. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this dance that makes use of alternating quarter turns. Its name is believed to come from a vaudeville performer who helped to make it popular.
The foxtrot was popularized by a couple with this last name, in part due to their role in Irving Berlin's Watch Your Step.
This faster dance combined the foxtrot with the charleston, and the leader closes their feet while dancing, unlike in the foxtrot.

bonuses.leadin: Dancers mostly close their feet at the end of each figure while performing this dance's American Social style, as opposed to passing them in its other two styles. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this longest reigning Chinese dynasty, which took power after Ji Fa won against the Shang dynasty at the Battle of Muye (moo-yuh).
The State of Lu's official chronicle, the Annals, provided the name for a "period" where the Eastern Zhou began named after two of these time periods-spring and autumn.

Sun Tzu wrote a military chronicle during the late Spring and Autumn period about "The Art of [this phenomenon]." The Zhou Dynasty collapsed in a period named for this phenomenon occurring between states.

bonuses.leadin: Philosophers like Confucius flourished during this dynasty's Hundred Schools of Thought. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this finest possible topology in which all subsets are open.

Any function from the discrete topology to another topological space always has this property because the pullback is always open. Functions with this property can be sketched without lifting the pencil from the paper.
The discrete topology has this property if it is finite. Topological spaces have this property if every open cover contains a finite subcover.

bonuses.leadin: The metric that is equal to 1 if x is not equal to y, and equal to 0 if x is equal to y induces this topology. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this English monarch, who was forced to agree to the Provisions of Oxford. The fractious Barons' Wars occurred during this man's reign.
This nobleman led resistance to Henry III during the Second Barons' War. He was slain in the battle of Evesham, and his body was carved up and sent to loyalist lords.
Henry III's son of this name led the royalist forces in smacking down Montfort at Evesham. This man, who later became king, was known as Longshanks, and opposed William Wallace.

bonuses.leadin: This monarch reportedly had a mural of Edward the Confessor painted in his bedchamber. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this organ. Cancer of this organ is typically diagnosed by inserting a camera into the anus, and this digestive organ ends in the rectum.
Colon cancer typically begins with these structures growing on the colon wall. These structures, which have 'sessile' and 'pedunculated' types, are small abnormal growths on a mucous membrane.
If colon cancer is allowed to develop, however, this phenomenon may occur, in which cancerous cells move from a tumour to other parts of the body, making it far harder to cure.

bonuses.leadin: Lynch syndrome is a genetic condition primarily associated with the cancer of this organ. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The active ingredient in bleach is this sodium salt with formula NaClO.
Sodium-hypochlorite combines with this other basic compound via the Olin-Raschig process to form hydrazine, a component of rocket fuel.
The highly exothermic reaction of sodium hypochlorite with hydrogen peroxide produces sodium-chloride, water, and this gas.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about the dangers of bleach For 10 points each.

parts.text: First, identify this central event within Islam that occurs on the eighth day of Dhul-Hijjah, which commemorates both the trials of Abraham and the flight of Mohammad to Mecca.
Upon arriving in Mecca, Muslim pilgrims circle this cube-shaped stone building in a counter-clockwise fashion and also kiss the black stone in the corner of this building.
After the hajj concludes, pilgrims, along with Muslims all over the world, celebrate this Feast of Sacrifice. This day of remembrance and forgiveness also sees gifts given to children.

bonuses.leadin: Practitioners of Islam are given a pass on adhering to this pillar if they have ill health or lack of money. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these organelles that are the site of translation.
Ribosomes can be found in prokaryotes because they do not have this property. Mitochondria have the "double" type of this property.
Distances in ribosomes are measured by using this unit, which is actually a measure of time equal to ten to the negative thirteen seconds.

bonuses.leadin: These organelles are found free floating in the cytoplasm in prokaryotes, while they are often bound to the rough endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this painting in which the ruins of the title structure, including an arch to the right and a support to the left, are all that remains of it.
The Bridge at Narni was painted by this leader of the Barbizon School who caused controversy with his depiction of Hagar in the Wilderness and showed a large, leafless tree in his Ville d'Avray.
Corot was a fan of this type of painting that showcases natural beauty, often featuring rivers, trees, and hills. Claude Lorrain and Nicolas Poussin also did paintings in this genre.

bonuses.leadin: The left and right sides of this painting are dominated by two large hills, the right of which is bathed in the darkness of its own shadow. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Central Asian country with capital at Nur-Sultan, renamed from Astana in 2019. It is the largest landlocked country in the world.

Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.

In addition to caviar, an industry revolving around this substance is prominent along the shores of the Caspian Sea. Due to its location on the lake, Iran produces 137.5 billion barrels of the "crude" form of this substance, which is often used to power cars.

bonuses.leadin: In 1997, this country moved its capital from Almaty, its largest city. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this party that nominated people such as Earl Dodge, John Bidwell and James Black, and supported the passage of the Volstead Act.
1933 saw the passage of this act which allowed manufacturers to produce 3.2% alcohol beer, preceding the December passage of the 21st amendment.

Howard Hyde Russell founded this temperance organization in Oberlin, Ohio in 1893. One notable member of this group, Wayne Wheeler, rode house to house on a bicycle to defeat a pro-alcohol state senator.

bonuses.leadin: The only time this political party nominated a candidate who won the presidency was in 1928 when it also nominated the Republican ticket of Hoover and Curtis. FTPE:
